chunks.heading: chapter 48 n a r e S earch Stu D y V I gne t te n n n 627
chunks.content:
like lines of code, whereas process metrics measure the efficiency of fault detection during
development. The project could have been directed to concentrate on scope and elapsed time.
Each type of metric measurement needing to be measured would be defined either using
internal or external attributes. Internal attributes are measured in terms of the entity itself.
External attributes represent a measure of the relationship to some external requirement
defined by the environment in which the entity is produced or used. For instances, software
code maintainability represents the ability of a specific product entity to adhere to accom-
modating changes in a reasonable manner. Another example is being able to modify the code
in one module without having to understand the code in another module.
It is likely that the study team would have decided that the study concentrate on attributes that
can be measured directly by examining the process, the product, and the resources applied.
Indirect measures can be obtained by establishing an empirical relationship between the
measure desired and other countable attributes of the entity. Counting man hours devoted
to a task is a direct measurement for the procedural design task. A module complexity attri-
bute can be determined indirectly through measuring other countable characteristics of the
software design logic such as the number of simple branch points in the algorithm. Then
complexity might simply be a function of the number of simple branches found in the code.
Process improvement through defect measurement and analyzes is facilitated by the nature
of the data collected. A modification of the Software Engineering Institute’s (SEI) Process
Maturity Model can be utilized. The usage of a nationally recognized standard lends validity
and reliability to the research study, especially internal validity and external validity.
Metrics can be chosen for each phase of the SDLC: specification, design, implementation
and integration, and maintenance. Time spent on specification development, size, effort, and
number of pages in the specification document could be used for the specification phase. The
number of modules as the size of the product, module cohesion and coupling as a measure of
the quality of the design, and fault statistics could be used for the design phase. Total num-
ber of test cases which result in a failure as well as other accurately kept fault statistics would
probably be utilized in the implementation phase. The metrics used for measurement in all
the other phases are pertinent to the metric measurements needed for the maintenance phase.
The discussion on screening for attributes implies that the research study would not have a
design but a collection of designs, indicated by the phases of the SDLC. In fact, the imple-

chunks.title: researchmethodsforinformationsystems
chunks.heading: chapter 48 n a r e S earch Stu D y V I gne t te n n n 627
chunks.content:
mentation phase might help the study team in integrating these phases. Now, the team
should consider the screening process for selecting a good design.
What precisely is a research design? First it is a plan, structure, and strategy of the inves-
tigation to be conducted. Planning is actually the overall scheme or programmed activities
of the research. Such an program of activities includes everything that must be done by the
researcher from writing the hypothesis(es) to the analysis(es) of the data. The outline, scheme,
and modeling of the operation of the variables specify the structure of the design. Strategy is

chunks.title: researchmethodsforinformationsystems
chunks.heading: chapter 48 n a r e S earch Stu D y V I gne t te n n n 629
chunks.content:
chapter 48 n a r e S earch Stu D y V I gne t te n n n 629
composed of the methods for data gathering and analyzing the data. How research objectives
are reached and how to tackle the research problems is the purpose of the strategy.
What is the purpose of a research design? Primarily the purpose is to obtain answers to
the research questions. Second, the research is to control variance. The major emphasis in
research is to get answers to the questions while controlling for experimental, extraneous,
and error variances for the research studied.
A research design enables the researcher to answer research questions: with validity, objec-
tively, accurately, and with economic control. Design does not inform the researcher on what
to do, rather the design infers the direction of observation-making and analysis. Acceptable
designs must address:
How many observations should be made?
Which variables are active?
Which variables are assigned?
Researchers need to be able to manipulate the active variables and categorize the assigned
variables. Additionally, the design tells the researcher what type of statistical analysis, and/
or other methodologies, to use. More importantly, an adequate design will outline possible
conclusions to be derived from the statistical design.
Note that in the computing field, projects are not just limited to statistical analysis but can
involve measurement, simulation, and analytic modeling. Often the emphasis of the research
may be dependent upon techniques of performance evaluation, workload characterization,
and benchmarking. Many such studies implement queuing network-based simulation mod-
els of computer systems. However, stochastic analysis can be used instead of using simula-
tion models of computer systems. Using these models for various computing platforms, the
research study goals, probably resolved with an experimental design, could be:
1. to compare a number of systems and decide which system is best for a given set of
applications,
2. to determine for a specific system how well it is performing and whether any
improvements need to be made.
The Design choice influences which method of analysis are needed.
For each one of the SDLC phases, should the design approached be experimental or nonex-
perimental? If an independent variable can be manipulated, then an experimental approach
can and should be used. The variables in this study are numerous and complex, which indi-
cates to the study team that both experimental and nonexperimental designs are required.
Every adequate design must answer:
Does the design answer the research questions?
Will the design enable testing the hypotheses?
Researchers must remember to solve problems, not just apply techniques.

chunks.content:
The main objective of any study is to resolve the answer to the question not just apply tech-
niques. The method or technique is secondary.
Design research to answer the research questions.
Does the design adequately control independent variables?
Randomize whenever possible.
Control independent variables [which limits systematic variance from extraneous
and unwanted sources to have presence in the study].
Remember that a perfectly good design can and is often poorly used.
A good design must possess both internal validity and external validity.
If experimental design is required, then other potential questions are:
Should factors be included, if so what are the pertinent factors?
How many levels of each factor should be included?
How should the levels of the factors be spaced?
How should the experimental units be selected?
How many experimental units should be chosen for each treatment combination?
What steps should be taken to control experimental error?
What criterion measures should be used to evaluate the effects of the treatment
factors?
What if a modeling approach had been decided upon? Before undertaking more elaborate
testing, a good approach is to begin looking for obvious errors or oversights in the model.
When screening and evaluating candidate models, the researcher can:
Determine whether or not the current candidate model reveals any such mistakes as based
upon the problem statement.
Determine if all mathematical expressions are consistent with the units the model uses.
By varying the input parameters and/or the predictor variables, decide whether or not the
output from the model behaves in a acceptable manner.
Perform retrospective tests on the model to check if good results are produced.
Whatever methodology is used, researchers must address the validity issue. Internal validity
asks the question: Does the experimental manipulation really make a statistically significant
difference? If the study results and design are representative, or generalizable, then the
study possesses external validity.
To what populations can the results be generalized?
Are the variables of this research representative?

48.8 r eporting r esults
The team has planned, and then re-planned many times. Additionally the team has prepared.
At this point it would be time for DOING: implement the plan, perform the analysis, and
convey the results. The study will have: finished data validation, possibly created new vari-
ables, selected variables for the final model, removed outliers, chosen the “best” model or
models, and introduced knowing how to process categorical variables. Most of these tasks
required many decisions to be made for which no clear cut rules existed.
Decisions have an impact on research results and must be justified.
Research must be shared [discussed] with interested communities.
When reporting results, the study team must be sure the reader understands the results.
Tell them what you are going to tell them, tell them again, and then tell them what
you told them once more.
Present the most important results first, then present decreasingly important results. For
each set of results, remind the reader what research question the result is answering. After
all research questions have been presented, present any qualifications or elaborations using
a similar order.
Each finding should be presented first in prose, second in numbers, and then again in prose.
In the main results section of the teams final report, limited interpretation of results is per-
missible, it prepares the reader for the conclusion section.
Conclusions should logically follow from results.
The first paragraph of the discussion section must include a restatement of the research
question. A discussion should also include the teams efforts to relate the results to previous
research on the topic.
Keep the discussion section as brief as possible.
Toward the end of the discussion section the team should present what the team believed to
be some questions that remain unanswered despite the efforts made by the research study
team. It could be that questions are raised because of the results obtained by the study.
The discussion section should not contain any surprises for the reader.
Don’t allow detours.

48.9 p romoting r esearch r esults
This section contains the main points of the complete report but none of the qualifications
and elaborations necessary to fully understand those main points. This section is a teaser.
Hopefully the reader will use the executive summary to decide whether or not to read and/
or study the full report.
Make the executive summary informative and brief.
How? Rewrite, then rewrite, and finally you may have to rewrite again.
48.10 v ignette c losing
As a runner it surprises people when they inform others that being fit or to maintain good

chunks.title: researchmethodsforinformationsystems
chunks.heading: chapter 48 n a r e S earch Stu D y V I gne t te n n n 631
chunks.content:
health are not why they are compulsive about running. Nor is it the acquisition of trophies and
competition that is important. Running is something they enjoy, something that they continu-
ously and perpetually practice on a consistent basis. Being a runner is part of one’s identity.
Suppose the study is completed. The reader has just witnessed and participated in extract-
ing knowledge from data. The reader should also have transferred the new knowledge to
other groups of individuals. Continue the journey by continuously performing a background
review, searching the Web, interacting with other researches in the study domain, and join-
ing a professional society and attending their conferences. Hopefully the reader will consider
not only enhancing their conceptual framework, but let research be part of their identity,
much as the runner claims identity with the “running lifestyle!”
48.11 c hapter s ummary
Research in the computing field evolved from ad hoc research to experimental research. ‘Ad
hoc’ research suffers from problems such as invalidity and irreproducibility. Use of experi-
mental designs, whenever possible, avoid these common pitfalls.
The breadth of the computing field includes: human factors research, operating systems,
computer systems organization, and data base management systems is only a short list. This
breadth of the field implies that researchers need to place an emphasis on measurement,
simulation, and analytical modeling as well as experimental research.
Additionally the reader has probably noticed the emphasis on project management in the
vignette. Technical projects are also business projects; they involve business issues such as
customer satisfaction, resource utilization, cost, profits, and many other business factors.
In the vignette the systems development cycle assumed as a framework for both the study
team and the project team. This framework can serve as a general scheme for illustrating
commonalities and differences among projects. Often individuals preparing for research are
either a technical person with little or no education in management or they are a person
primarily involved in product-development, marketing, process improvement, or related

chunks.heading: chapter 48 n a r e S earch Stu D y V I gne t te n n n 633
chunks.content:
chapter 48 n a r e S earch Stu D y V I gne t te n n n 633
projects, with limited background in technology. These individuals need to embark on a
study of project management.
Participants in research projects need to develop an appreciation for both the project man-
agement and the human and organizational side as well. Successful projects are those where
good communications, mutual trusts, and teamwork are present.
48.12 e xercises
Various types of research questions are represented in the following list.
a. For each question you are to determine if the actual computing environment, use of
simulation, or an analytic model should be used in the study.
b. Using this model describe how to resolve the research question based upon your
answer to Part A. The following list of activities may provide guidance in answering:
n design sets of experiments for measurement or simulation.
n check if the model is adequate.
n make comparative performance analyzes for the alternatives.
n control for measurement errors.
1. A performance evaluation for a personal workstation. To design this worksta-
tion answer: Which processor should be chosen? How much memory should
be recommended? How many external CD drives should be recommended?
Assume the workload can be of three types: secretarial, management, or
scientific. Also assume the end-user is either novice or expert. This is a system
design problem.
2. Determine the best database management system for a social work office infor-
mation referral system for seven counties for social services for senior citizens.
Consideration should be given to cost, availability, and compatibility. (Hint:
Look into required workloads and benchmarks). This is a system selection
problem.
3. Find for your organization about the current computing system. Consider a
system upgrade study. Either replacing the whole system or parts of the current
system with newer but compatible units. Assume the compatibility consider-
ations are dictated by the vendor. You are to recommend quantity, speed, and
other pertinent attribute values.
4. For the DBMS application in problem (2) using the required workload using
appropriate attributes and the social work office resource management policies,
optimize the performance of the query and data manipulation processing. This
is a system tuning problem.
634 n n n r e S earch Metho DS F or In F or M at I on Sy S te MS n ch apter 48
5. Your office workstation is unacceptably sluggish. Develop a method to deter-
mine whether inadequate resources of poor system management is the reason.
You can monitor the system and examine the behavior of various resource man-
agement policies under different loading conditions. This is a system analysis
problem.
6. Your company is considering the expansion of an existing computing facility.

chunks.heading: chapter 48 n a r e S earch Stu D y V I gne t te n n n 633
chunks.content:
Discuss how measurements under the real workload can be utilized to solve this
problem. Consider the case where direct measurements are possible and when
only indirect measurements are available. Note that workload characterization
only builds a model of the real workload.
7. Compare the effect of ORACLE, ACCESS, and SYSBASE on user perfor-
mance. This is a relational data modeling problem.
8. Determine how data technicians organize data, and if they are capable of
organizing data into lists, hierarchies, tables, and networks. This is a data model
problem.
9. Explore the difference in novice and expert users’ performance in searching,
storing, and retrieving information from a database. This is a human factors
study.
10. Test the assertion that many of the existing optimizing cluster techniques per-
form as well or better than JAN in clustering the policies of a group of raters
or judges. Hint: use a Monte Carlo simulation. Number of policies, raters, and
number of raters per policy should be varied and analyzed with an appropriate
experimental design.
